candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — supporting self-management in the home environment
candidate.educational_objective: Support medication adherence by identifying individual barriers and making the regimen easier to follow through clinically appropriate schedule simplification, daily routines, and reminder tools.

options.A: Keep the current complex dosing schedule unchanged and add extra written instructions, without exploring whether the number of daily dosing times can be reduced.
options.B: Teach the medication purposes and directions, but avoid asking about side effects, cost, confusion, or other factors that may make the regimen difficult to follow.
options.C: Identify the client's barriers, simplify or cluster dosing times when clinically possible, link doses to daily routines, and use a pill organizer or electronic reminder if helpful.
options.D: Ask the client to rely on memory rather than routines or reminder tools so that adherence does not become dependent on external prompts.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ Tool 16 recommends asking what makes medication use difficult, considering options that reduce the number of daily doses when clinically appropriate, linking medication-taking to regular daily activities, and using pill organizers or electronic reminders when useful. Therefore C directly addresses both the complex schedule and forgetting. A leaves the complexity unaddressed, B intentionally fails to assess common adherence barriers, and D rejects reminder strategies specifically recommended by AHRQ.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Medication-management support includes identifying barriers, reducing dosing frequency or clustering medicines when clinically appropriate, linking doses to daily routines, and using pill organizers or electronic reminders to help patients remember medicines.
